papers.title: Purpose-Bounded Context Exchange in Enterprise Agentic AI Systems: An Inter-Module Information Contract Architecture
papers.summary: Enterprise agentic AI systems exchange contextual information across functional modules, creating governance challenges when information crosses operational and organizational boundaries. This study distinguishes organizational governance boundaries from information exchange boundaries and proposes an Inter-Module Information Contract (IMIC) architecture for purpose-bounded context exchange. IMIC evaluates provenance, semantic and temporal validity, permitted information scope, and applicable originating constraints before downstream execution, independently of language-model reasoning. We compare IMIC with full-context sharing, reduced-context sharing, and strengthened structured handoff. In a deterministic benchmark of 32 synthetic conditions, joint correctness is achieved in 3, 10, 28, and 32 cases, respectively. The four differences between strengthened structured handoff and IMIC arise from conditions testing onward-transfer permission, recipient, purpose, and field scope. A downstream integration experiment evaluates 14 selected conditions across four local language models and three seeds, yielding 168 case–model–seed blocks and 672 method-level records. IMIC achieves correct exchange actions and information boundaries in all 168 blocks and joint correctness in 165 across four local LLMs and three seeds. papers.title: Adaptive Mutual–Human Reflection: A Universal Framework for Multi-LLM Reciprocal Reflection, Human Metacognitive Participation, and Context-Aware Switching
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly employ reflection mechanisms to inspect their own outputs, identify potential errors, reconsider intermediate decisions, and improve subsequent responses. Recent research has also demonstrated the potential of multi-agent debate, collaborative critique, and human feedback for improving the quality of artificial intelligence systems. However, reflection in intelligent systems remains substantially fragmented across self-reflection, multi-agent interaction, external evaluation, and human feedback. In particular, an important architectural question remains: should a system rely on reciprocal reflection among multiple LLMs, human reflection, or a dynamically coordinated combination of both, and how should it determine when to transition between these mechanisms? This paper introduces Adaptive Mutual–Human Reflection (AMHR), a theoretical framework developed as a function-specific extension of the Universal Mutual-Human Model (UMHM). AMHR establishes two fundamental reflection dimensions: Mutual Reflection (M), in which two or more distinct LLMs reciprocally examine, challenge, interpret, and revise one another's reasoning and conclusions; and Human Reflection (H), in which human individuals or groups independently examine and reconsider the assumptions, reasoning, evidence, judgments, and outcomes of an intelligent system. papers.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
papers.summary: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

papers.title: Fare Calculation Methodology in Automated Public Transport Payment Systems: Zoning, Per-kilometer, and Adaptive Tariffs
papers.summary: The purpose of the research is to develop proposals for tariff setting in automated fare collection systems for public transport. The work focuses on a critical analysis of the zonal fare model currently operating in the Leningrad region. The study analyzed 760 routes in the Leningrad region. Key shortcomings of the existing approach were identified: the violation of the principle of payment proportionality for the provided transport service, due to the discrete nature of the tariff model, which forces passengers into suboptimal behavioral scenarios; cost inequity on parallel routes; and a conflict of interest between transport companies and consumers of transport services when determining tariff zone boundaries. To overcome the identified problems, a number of alternative tariff models are proposed. An approach to the algorithmic determination of the number and boundaries of tariff zones is described, utilizing fuzzy logic and multi-criteria optimization that accounts for the specifics of the route network and transportation demand patterns. A strategy for transitioning to a per-kilometer fare is developed, involving the modernization of the automated fare collection system to overcome existing technical limitations. papers.title: Strategic Evaluation and Implementation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Price Volatility in the Steel Commodity Market: A Comparative Study with the Foreign Exchange Market for Commercial Decision-Making
papers.summary: This study aimed to implement and strategically compare machine-learning and deep-learning models for predicting price volatility in the Iranian steel commodity market and the EUR/USD foreign-exchange market and to evaluate their usefulness for commercial decision-making. This applied-developmental study used a descriptive-analytical design based on secondary time-series data from January 2019 to January 2024. The foreign-exchange dataset included hourly and daily EUR/USD opening, high, low, closing, and volume data extracted from MetaTrader 5. The steel dataset included daily and weekly prices of steel billets and sheets traded on the Iran Mercantile Exchange, together with the unofficial exchange rate, global 62% iron-ore prices, and seasonal demand indicators. After outlier correction, linear interpolation, logarithmic differencing, and feature engineering, Random Forest, XGBoost, Long Short-Term Memory, and Deep Q-Network models were implemented. Model validation was conducted through walk-forward validation using a three-year training window and a one-year out-of-sample testing window. Predictive and strategic performance were assessed through forecasting errors, directional accuracy, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, win rate, and profit factor. papers.title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem explorer prototype
papers.summary: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. Rather than treating excited-state dynamics simulations as isolated results reported in heterogeneous formats and across different sources, PCE organizes studies according to their molecular systems, computational workflows, methodological choices, and associated observables, facilitating that relationships and trends can be explored systematically across studies. In this way, the prototype illustrates how structured data representations could support improved findability, comparison, reproducibility, and reuse in computational photochemistry. At a fundamental level, it demonstrates how excited-state dynamics studies could become part of a more connected and cumulative body of knowledge, potentially enabling new modes of investigation. The prototype exposes practical challenges that must be addressed to realize this vision, including the development of shared representations, workflow descriptions, and their integration into scientific practice. More broadly, PCE is intended as a practice-driven experimentation platform to stimulate discussion and iterative community development of standards and representations for excited-state dynamics studies.

papers.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance. This study evaluated the capacity of Iran’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to support responsible AI governance by reconstructing its underlying program theory and examining the coherence of its implementation architecture. The research adopted a qualitative, theory-based case-study design. Data were obtained through documentary analysis of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and related policy materials, together with semi-structured interviews with 12 experts from academic, research, policy, and industrial backgrounds. The data were coded and thematically analysed using MAXQDA, after which an integrated theory of change and theory of action was developed and applied to the national strategy. The findings indicated that responsible AI governance in Iran depends on sustained political commitment, a legally empowered and agile coordinating institution, equitable access to high-quality data and computational infrastructure, interdisciplinary human capital, effective university–industry collaboration, risk-based regulation, and continuous policy evaluation. The strategy provides an important normative foundation by emphasizing human dignity, national values, scientific development, priority sectors

papers.title: A roadmap for polymer informatics superintelligence
papers.summary: Polymer informatics has matured from isolated property-prediction studies into an integrated discipline that couples data, models, and decision-making across the polymer design cycle. Yet it still falls short of a true intelligent system capable of inverse design on demand, causal reasoning across chemistry, processing, and performance, and closed-loop autonomous experimentation. This article traces a roadmap toward that goal, grounded in experience developing two complementary agentic and informatics platforms. Central to this vision is a modular, agent-directed architecture in which a polymer superintelligence layer interprets a researcher’s design question in natural language and coordinates domain-specialized tools, matched to the available data, for neat polymers, composites and formulations, solvents, and synthesis and processing. The resulting system spans the full chain from molecular design through processing to product-level performance and human perception. Orchestrated together, its generative design, synthesis-feasibility reasoning, and practicality assessment already form the decision-making core of a self-driving polymer laboratory, leaving autonomous, closed-loop experimentation as the principal step that remains. papers.title: NeuroImgAgent: a multi-agent platform for cross-species fMRI analysis with evidence-gated quality control
papers.summary: Cross-species functional MRI analysis requires coordinating specialized workflows and assessing intermediate outputs. We present NeuroImgAgent, a multi-agent platform driven by large language models that translates natural-language requests into workflows for humans, macaques, rats and mice. Quantitative checks and vision-language model assessments determine whether processing continues, enters bounded recovery or stops. Across 268 paired cases, preprocessing metrics were broadly comparable to those of fMRIPrep, AFNI and RABIES. With GPT-5.5, NeuroImgAgent corrected 111 of 120 induced orientation errors and passed all 52 intent-recognition and planning tasks, 8 of 9 recovery tasks and 11 of 14 tool-construction tasks on NeuroAgentBench. In 120 paired challenge cases, the full configuration increased usability from 76.7% to 92.5%, as assessed by blinded experts, and reduced unusable outputs delivered without warning from 18.3% to 4.2% of cases relative to quality-control ablation.

papers.summary: This study aims to dissect the epistemological roots of political stagnation in Afghanistan by examining the dialectical tension between “modern posited rationality” and “premodern traditional legitimacy” during the period from 2001 to 2021. The central research question is based on the proposition of how the “regime of truth of tradition” was able to assimilate and transform the modern signifiers of modernization within civil and legal institutions, thereby generating “discursive entropy” in the state-building project. The research employs Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), drawing upon Norman Fairclough’s three-dimensional model and Michel Foucault’s genealogical approach. The findings indicate that political modernization in post-2001 Afghanistan was reduced to a formalistic and artificially sustained process due to the incongruity between the “text of modern law” and the “traditional habitus of social agents.” The analysis demonstrates that civil and educational institutions, such as universities and the judiciary, rather than functioning as centers of transition toward Weberian rationality and a Habermasian public sphere, became arenas for the reproduction of ethnic solidarities and rigid jurisprudential interpretations. papers.title: Independent Learning after Generative AI Support in School Mathematics: A Systematic Review and Assessment-Stratified Meta-Analysis
papers.summary: Background and Objective. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solves school math problems on demand. Higher scores during live tool access do not prove retained mathematical competence once that support disappears. Earlier meta-analyses pooled assisted task completion together with unmonitored and closed-book posttests, which obscured whether pupils actually learned to work alone. This PRISMA 2020 systematic review and stratified meta-analysis evaluates K–12 mathematics outcomes by separating test-time resource rules from instructional design. Methods. Two-stream searches across ERIC, APA PsycNet, OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, EuropePMC, and bidirectional citation chasing (1 January 2022–8 November 2026) returned 11,061 raw entries and 6,530 unique records. Every sought report was retrieved in full (372 / 372; 0 unretrieved). Eligibility verification and mathematical consistency checks retained 49 K–12 school-mathematics reports across 46 independent cohorts and supplied 36 quantitative contrasts across 20 controlled study families (21 controlled quantitative reports, plus 1 factorial within-AI modality trial synthesized narratively) alongside 28 qualitative, single-arm, observational, and boundary-comparator reports. papers.title: Body Form and Architectural Elements for Conservation-Led Daylight Optimization in Cultural Museum: A Case Study of Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria
papers.summary: Daylight is a valued architectural resource in museum design, yet uncontrolled daylight exposes cultural artifacts to fading, embrittlement, colour change, ultraviolet degradation, glare, and thermal stress.This exploratory article examines how the body form and architectural elements of a cultural museum in Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria, can optimize daylight while protecting light-sensitive artifacts. Using an exploratory, mixed-methods, design-based approach, and the study integrates literature review, climate and site analysis, cultural heritage assessment, case-study review, and daylight-performance simulation. The article proposes a “Sheltered Grove of Memory” concept: a compact, clustered museum form in which bright public and circulation spaces are separated from low-light, conservation-controlled galleries. The proposed strategy uses deep-plan gallery cores, shaded courtyards, high-level clerestories, roof monitors, light wells, external shading fins, light shelves, diffusing ceilings, ultraviolet-filtered glazing, and automated shading. Conservation thresholds guide the design: a maximum of approximately 50 lux for highly sensitive artifacts, 150–200 lux for moderately sensitive artifacts, and up to 300 lux for durable materials such as stone, ceramic, and metal. papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for design in emerging creative environments
papers.summary: The study, titled From Artificial Intelligence: Competencies for Design in Emerging Creative Environments, aims to determine the competencies linked to the use of Artificial Intelligence in the training of designers, as well as to examine its impact on the professional environment. The advancement of AI has reconfigured not only the tools for design practice, but also the essential dynamics of the creative process. In emerging human-AI collaboration [HAIC] scenarios, these systems operate as cooperative agents and not merely as support tools. However, even though design students are progressively incorporating these technologies into their practice, a gap persists in the development of fundamental competencies for establishing effective interaction with these systems. Therefore, the need to strengthen disciplinary training through competencies that integrate critical interpretation, collaborative interaction, ethical and metacognitive reflection, in addition to specialized technical mastery is recognized. Based on the above, this research is structured around a comprehensive review of scientific literature, analysing studies retrieved from specialized databases in both design and higher education. The methodology will adopt the PRISMA [2021] systematic review protocol, which will ensure a rigorous process for the identification, selection, and synthesis of emerging competencies

papers.title: When Human Assurance Matters: Task Complexity and Pre-Interaction Expected Satisfaction in Human-AI Hybrid Service Systems
papers.summary: Consumers frequently disengage from AI service encounters because they doubt whether chatbots can resolve their requests. Although human–AI hybrid systems provide human backup, this capability is often concealed. Drawing on Uncertainty Reduction Theory and Cognitive Appraisal Theory, we examine when human assurance—an upfront statement that users may transfer to a human if the AI cannot resolve the request—improves pre-interaction expectations. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 217) and a within-subject EEG experiment (N = 35) show that assurance increases expected system capability and expected satisfaction, with larger effects under high task complexity. Expected system capability mediates this relationship. EEG results reveal early frontal theta synchronization followed by later frontal alpha desynchronization under high complexity, a temporal pattern consistent with affective engagement and cognitive elaboration. These findings identify human assurance as a task-contingent cue that makes hybrid systems’ recourse capability visible.

papers.title: Reconstructing The Concept Of Self Actualisation In Artificial Intelligence Based Learning : An Integrative Literature Review
papers.summary: The development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has transformed the learning ecology by positioning AI as a cognitive partner that supports personalisation, feedback, problem-solving, and creativity. This transformation necessitates a reconstruction of the concept of self-actualisation, as some human cognitive activities can be delegated to AI. This study aims to analyse the transformation of self actualisation, identify the conditions that strengthen or hinder it, and formulate a conceptual framework for self-actualisation in AI-based learning. This study employs a qualitative library research approach using an integrative literature review design. The findings indicate that GenAI is paradoxical in nature: it can serve as a cognitive scaffold that strengthens autonomy, competence, self-regulation, creativity, metacognition, and epistemic agency, while also potentially encouraging cognitive offloading, dependence, and the weakening of cognitive autonomy. This study proposes the Reflective-Relational Self Actualisation Framework in AI Learning Ecologies (RRSA-AILE), which encompasses autonomy, competence, relatedness, epistemic agency, metacognitive reflexivity, generative creativity, and ethical responsibility. papers.title: EgoPlay: Event-Triggered Video Editing for Egocentric Streams
papers.summary: We introduce EgoPlay, an event-triggered video-to-video editor for egocentric streams, obtained by fine-tuning a pretrained V2V diffusion transformer on event-conditioned data built primarily from Ego4D. Given a monocular video and an event-triggered prompt of the form “when X happens, do Y,” EgoPlay infers whether and when event X occurs, preserves pre-event frames, and applies edit Y only to the post-event continuation. Rather than cascading a separate event detector with an editor, EgoPlay learns event recognition, temporal restraint, and pixel-level editing jointly in a single end-to-end model, while also handling negative and multi-event prompts. To support this, we construct a large-scale dataset of 106K event-triggered clip–prompt pairs spanning positive triggers, fabricated-trigger negatives, and multi-event prompts. We then train a bidirectional video diffusion editor with event-triggered supervision and derive a causal variant for chunk-by-chunk streamable inference. We further introduce an event-aware evaluation protocol that separately measures post-trigger editing quality, pre-trigger preservation, and false-trigger robustness. papers.title: The Governance Frontier COBIT-Aligned AI Decision Support and Risk-Adaptive Optimization for Enterprise Technology Modernization
papers.summary: Executives deciding enterprise modernization, legacy-system transformation, AI adoption, organizational restructuring, digital-infrastructure change, and cross-functional governance must weigh legal, financial, cybersecurity, procurement, opera-tional, and AI-governance questions that sit in separate functions. The central methods of this paper are GAIM-DF (Governance-Aware Institutional Modernization Decision Framework), a human-gated advisory process for these decisions, and Risk-Adaptive AI Governance Optimization (RA-GO v2), a risk-adaptive optimizer with mandatory governance gates, halt-safe feasibility, distributionally robust evaluation, and preference-information triage for scarce human review; an accountable human decides. As an optional architectural extension, we compu-tationally evaluate a multi-expert coordination layer that convenes specialist capabilities by context and consolidates constraints conservatively. Evidence is staged across four complementary pre-deployment approaches: analytical verification; retrospective historical-data analysis; comparative computational benchmark-ing against strong baselines; and scenario-based stress testing under distributional shift. Together they provide complementary pre-deployment evidence for high-stakes governance analysis. A systematic review of university and public-sector governance, with observational process-log anal

papers.title: Human-first learning: scaffolding reasoning before AI assistance improves diagnostic accuracy
papers.summary: Generative AI could improve physicians' clinical performance, yet its use in medical training raises questions about whether trainees can develop the clinical reasoning needed to use AI effectively and independently. We conducted a longitudinal randomised controlled trial involving 496 medical students (389 analysed). Students completed clinical reasoning tasks with virtual standardised patients and were randomised to six conditions: no intervention, an AI assistant alone, AI scaffolding alone, scaffolding followed by the AI assistant, the AI assistant followed by scaffolding, or both simultaneously. AI scaffolding prompted students to reflect on and evaluate their reasoning without providing direct answers; the assistant provided requested information and answers. The study comprised an AI-free baseline, two intervention phases and a final assessment after all AI support was withdrawn. Frontier large language models (LLMs) completed the same tasks as an additional benchmark. Students initially performed below LLMs but later exceeded them following the interventions. Students who began with AI scaffolding achieved higher diagnostic accuracy than those given access to the AI assistant from the outset both during the subsequent intervention phase (75.2% vs 66.0%; OR 1.73, 95% CIs [1.12–2.68]) and after withdrawal (24.6% vs 14.4%; OR 2.19, 95% CIs [1.15–4.14]). papers.title: Lived experiences of relationships to generative AI mental health chatbots among adults
papers.summary: Nigeria’s mental health system serves less than 10% of those in need, with severe provider shortages and deep-seated stigma. Generative AI chatbots offer scalable support, yet how Nigerian adults experience attachment to non-human therapeutic agents remains unexplored. To examine lived experiences of AI therapeutic relationships among Nigerian adults, focusing on attachment formation, cultural acceptability, and perceived authenticity within contexts of care scarcity. Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis with 37 adults (18–45 years) who engaged AI mental health chatbots for ≥ 4 weeks. Semi-structured interviews explored relational experiences, trust development, privacy concerns, and comparisons with human/traditional healing. papers.title: A Brick in the Creative Wall: The Cultural and Creative Production System Facing the Challenge of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly transforming cultural and creative industries (CCIs), yet research lacks a structured understanding of how they intervene across production processes. How and where does GenAI reshape value creation activities within the CCI production system? Building on the UNESCO cultural cycle (2009), we develop an analytical framework that maps GenAI applications across three phases of the cultural production value chain: creation, production, and distribution/consumption. It identifies how GenAI reconfigures value creation and value capture mechanisms differently across phases and sectors. Our analysis highlights emerging dynamics, including phase-specific technological dependencies, increasing feedback loops between production and consumption, and a growing technological convergence across CCIs. To illustrate these mechanisms, we present cases from Galleries, Libraries, Archives and Museums (GLAM). Our paper contributes to ongoing debates on digital transformation in cultural production systems, providing insights for researchers, policymakers, and cultural organizations navigating the opportunities and risks of GenAI. JEL Codes: H0, M0, M1, O4

papers.title: A Comprehensive Overview of Bacopa monnieri Taxonomy, Constituents, Bioactivities, Herbal Formulations and Clinical Trials
papers.summary: B. monnieri, an herbal plant also referred to as brahmi, is an herb with medicinal and pharmacological active plant in traditional Indian medicinal history which has been broadly used in the an ancient ayurveda for improving memory, cognitive function, and neurological health. Brahmi is an ancient medicinal plant which used to prepare herbal formulations like brahmi ghritam, brahmi rasadi tailam, bacognize®, and bacomind®, which traditionally use in India for enhance memory and cognitive functions. This article provides a complete overview of B. monnieri taxonomy, ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemical constituents and their bioactivities, herbal formulation and clinical trials. Recent clinical trial studies identified the cognitive, neurological, and physiological effects of B. monnieri which act as the scientific evidence proving its therapeutic potential. papers.title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in psychologically informed musculoskeletal rehabilitation: A con-vergent mixed-methods investigation and the triadic care model

papers.title: Title Pending 10324
papers.summary: The extraordinary success of recent Large Language Models (LLMs) on a diverse array of tasks has led to an explosion of scientific and philosophical theorizing aimed at explaining how they do what they do. Unfortunately, disagreement over fundamental theoretical issues has led to stalemate, with entrenched camps of LLM optimists and pessimists often committed to very different views of how these systems work. Overcoming stalemate requires agreement on fundamental questions, and the goal of this paper is to address one such question, namely: is LLM behavior driven partly by representation-based information processing of the sort implicated in biological cognition, or is it driven entirely by processes of memorization and stochastic table look-up? This is a question about what kind of algorithm LLMs implement, and the answer carries serious implications for higher level questions about whether these systems have beliefs, intentions, concepts, knowledge, and understanding. I argue that LLM behavior is partially driven by representation-based information processing, and then I describe and defend a series of practical techniques for investigating these representations and developing explanations on their basis. The resulting account provides a groundwork for future theorizing about language models and their successors.

papers.title: Adapting HR Strategies to Enhance CRM in Aviation: A Qualitative Study on Emerging Technologies Grounded in Socio-Technical Systems Theory
papers.summary: Purpose –This study aims to explore how Human Resource Management (HRM) strategies can enhance Crew Resource Management (CRM) effectiveness in the context of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) in aviation. While these technologies improve operational efficiency, they also highlight the critical need for maintaining human oversight and decision-making processes.Design/methodology/approach –The research employs a qualitative methodology grounded in Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory. Data were collected through interviews with 15 aviation experts, including pilots, HR professionals, and operations managers, and analyzed using thematic analysis with NVivo software.Results–The findings indicate that while automation significantly enhances operational efficiency, maintaining manual skills and human decision-making remains essential for sustainable operations. The study also identifies the need for HR strategies to adapt to technological change through enhanced training programs, continuous learning initiatives, and revised recruitment practices.Discussion –This study contributes to STS theory by emphasizing the importance of balancing technological and social systems to ensure effective CRM in aviation.
